record.paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
record.original_question: For LINC-NIRVANA multiple-image deconvolution with Poisson data, what regularization methods based on sparse representations in an appropriate basis or frame can improve reconstruction of complex astronomical objects beyond the regularization functions already tested for simpler objects such as open star clusters, nebulae, distant galaxies, and planetary surfaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a Fizeau interferometric imaging system that produces, for a fixed astronomical target, a finite collection of blurred noisy images g_1,...,g_p : Ω → ℕ acquired with different orientations of the telescope baseline (so that each image has an anisotropic point spread function with high resolution along one direction and low resolution perpendicular to it). For each j = 1,...,p the data model is

   g_j = P(A_j x + b_j),

where x : Ω → ℝ_{≥0} is the unknown nonnegative object, A_j is the linear convolution operator with the known PSF K_j of the j-th acquisition, b_j ≥ 0 is the known background, and P(·) denotes Poisson sampling of its (nonnegative) intensity argument pixelwise. The negative log-likelihood (Csiszár I-divergence) to be minimized is

   J_0(x) = Σ_{j=1}^{p} Σ_{n ∈ Ω} { (A_j x + b_j)(n) − g_j(n) log[(A_j x + b_j)(n)] }.

Regularized reconstructions are obtained by minimizing F(x) = J_0(x) + μ R(x) over x ≥ 0, where R is a regularization functional and μ > 0.

Known classes of regularizers R that have been tested for the targets listed below include Tikhonov (quadratic) penalties, edge-preserving smoothness penalties, total variation, and Markov-type penalties; these have been validated on simulated reconstructions of:
 (i) open star clusters (point-like sources on a smooth background);
 (ii) diffuse nebulae;
 (iii) distant galaxies with smooth surface brightness profiles;
 (iv) planetary surfaces (piecewise-smooth extended objects).

Problem. Identify regularization functionals R(x) built from sparse representations of x in a suitable basis or frame (for example, wavelets, curvelets, shearlets, learned dictionaries, or other redundant frames adapted to astronomical morphologies) such that the corresponding minimizer of F provides quantitatively improved reconstructions—in terms of reconstruction error, dynamic range, and recovery of fine structure—for complex astronomical scenes (i.e., scenes simultaneously containing point-like sources, extended diffuse emission, and sharp edges, going beyond targets (i)–(iv)) under the multi-image Poisson model above. Provide such functionals together with provably convergent minimization algorithms compatible with the nonnegativity constraint and the Poisson likelihood.
artifact.category_tag: Poisson image deconvolution with sparse regularization
artifact.status_search_result: General-purpose sparse-representation regularizers for Poisson deconvolution (wavelet/framelet l1 priors, learned dictionaries, Anscombe-stabilized sparsity methods) have been developed in the broader imaging literature, and follow-up works on multi-image Poisson deblurring for LBT-like configurations (e.g., high dynamic-range scenes) continue to appear. However, no work definitively identifies a sparse-representation regularization scheme that is established as the method of choice for complex astronomical objects in the LINC-NIRVANA multi-image Fizeau setting; the question is best classified as open.

status_evidence.title: Image Deconvolution Under Poisson Noise Using Sparse Representations and Proximal Thresholding Iteration
status_evidence.snippet: Formulates Poisson deconvolution as minimization of a convex functional with data-fidelity term and l1 sparsity-promoting penalties over image representation coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Sparse-representation regularizers for Poisson deconvolution exist in general imaging, but not specialized/validated for the LINC-NIRVANA multi-image complex-object setting.

status_evidence.title: Multiple Image Deblurring with High Dynamic-Range Poisson Data
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multi-image Poisson deblurring relevant to LBT-like configurations with high dynamic range.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-image Poisson deblurring for LBT-like configurations remains an active research area.

status_evidence.title: Poissonian Image Deconvolution via Sparse and Redundant Representations and Framelet Regularization
status_evidence.snippet: Combines learned-dictionary sparse priors with framelet analysis priors for Poisson image deconvolution.
status_evidence.claim: Various sparse/framelet regularizers exist in the literature but were not benchmarked on LINC-NIRVANA complex-object simulations.
